summary: FireGuard SI is an insights dashboard that turns NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data into practical fire-safety guidance for spacecraft crews and mission designers. In microgravity there is no buoyancy: flames are spherical, smoke does not rise, and fire spreads only where ventilation pushes it, so lessons from Earth do not transfer. We pulled 26 PSI combustion investigations (Saffire I-III, BASS/BASS-II, FLEX/FLEX-2, SAME, ACME, CFI and more; 1,883 test points) into one searchable explorer, built a flame-spread estimator anchored on measured Saffire and BASS results, and connected both to a live ISS Mission Monitor: sensor fusion detects fire precursors, predicts fire probability and spread to neighbouring modules, and an SI crew advisor tells the crew what to do, citing the NASA experiment behind every step. It addresses the challenge directly: SI-powered, data-driven fire-safety insights from microgravity combustion data, for the ISS today and for Artemis/Gateway and Mars habitats tomorrow.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. FireGuard SI has four connected views. (1) PSI Research Explorer ranks 26 NASA PSI combustion investigations by fire-safety relevance, with full-text search, side-by-side comparison and a chart of every PSI test point (O2 vs. pressure) against exploration habitat atmospheres (ISS, Gateway, Artemis lander, Mars). It highlights data gaps: conditions future missions will fly that no experiment has tested yet. (2) Flammability Lab estimates flame spread for a material, O2, pressure, air flow and gravity (microgravity, Moon, Mars, Earth), anchored on Saffire-II measurements (2.1-2.6 mm/s for SIBAL cotton-fiberglass at 20 cm/s, ~22% O2) and BASS findings (flames self-extinguish below a minimum flow), and shows the nearest real PSI test points. (3) Mission Monitor simulates 8 ISS modules with 10 sensors each (smoke, CO, PM2.5, temperature, O2, CO2, HCN, rack power, pressure, ventilation). A random incident develops precursors; sensor fusion separates a real fire from a single faulty sensor and shows danger %, fire probability and fire involvement % live. Fire spreads to neighbouring modules through open hatches within 1-3 minutes unless the crew acts. Normal and special (ICCD 350-470 nm) camera views show hot flames and invisible cool flames as seen in NASA FLEX. (4) The SI Crew Advisor gives prevention steps during precursors, firefighting steps during a fire and post-fire atmosphere checks; every step cites its source (a PSI investigation or a NASA lesson learned such as Mir 1997 or Apollo 1). Crew actions (ventilation off, power off, extinguisher, hatch close) change the simulation using PSI physics, e.g. ventilation shutdown starves the flame, as BASS showed.

IMPACT. Fire is one of the most dangerous emergencies in spaceflight, and microgravity fire behaves unlike fire on Earth. Decades of NASA experiments exist but are hard to find and compare. FireGuard SI makes that knowledge usable in seconds by crews, mission planners and habitat designers, and points to where new experiments are needed for Artemis, Gateway and Mars.

TOOLS. HTML, CSS and JavaScript front end with Chart.js; Node.js and Express server; Node data pipeline that downloads PSI investigation metadata and data tables from psi.nasa.gov and builds a JSON data set and a text knowledge base; BM25 retrieval; optional Claude API for natural-language answers grounded in NASA sources (a fully offline rule engine works without any key); English and Russian interface.

CREATIVITY AND HONEST LIMITS. Instead of a static report, the PSI data drives a live what-if monitor where crew choices visibly change the outcome, and every recommendation is traceable to a NASA experiment. Limitations: sensor data and cabin camera footage are simulated (labelled in the app); the spread estimator is an engineering estimate, not a certified model; it is decision support only, crew and Mission Control procedures take precedence.

SI DISCLOSURE. The 48 cabin camera clips (normal and ICCD views) are SI-generated videos rendered with Claude (Anthropic); each feed shows a visible "SI-GENERATED VIDEO" watermark in the app. Code was written with Claude as a coding assistant; all NASA data, physics anchors and citations were checked against the original NASA sources.
